note: Big merit scholarships that only go to students applying to one particular college, shown in the Financial Aid section of that college's profile. Each fact is the site's own wording of what its sources say; each source's evidence lines are that page's exact wording, and scripts/check-pathways.mjs confirms they are still there. Deadlines are for students entering in fall 2027. A college with no entry gets no card.

facts.text: Eight semesters of full tuition, room and board and most fees, plus funding for up to three summers.

sources.label: Robertson FAQs
evidence: provides eight semesters of full tuition, room and board, and most mandatory fees
Scholars also have access to generous funding for up to three summer experiences

facts.text: It's a separate application, due Nov 15, on top of your Duke application. Students of any citizenship can apply.

sources.label: Robertson: high school students
evidence: The application opens annually on the 15th of August and is due on the 15th of November.
There is one application for all High School students regardless of nationality or citizenship.

facts.text: You're only considered at the schools you apply to. Apply to both Duke and UNC to be considered at both.

sources.label: Robertson FAQs
evidence: a student who applies to both universities will be considered for the Robertson at both universities
will only be considered for the Robertson at UNC-Chapel Hill

facts.text: Four years of full tuition, housing and meals, books and mandatory fees, plus a civic engagement grant and four summer experiences.

sources.label: Levine Scholars: what it includes
evidence: The four-year scholarship includes: Full Tuition Housing and Meals Books Mandatory Fees Civic Engagement Grant Four Summer Experiences

facts.text: Apply to NC State and to Park by 11:59pm ET on Nov 1. You need a 3.80 unweighted GPA, and you must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident or graduating from a U.S. high school.

Have a minimum unweighted GPA of 3.80 (non-rounded).
Be a United States citizen, permanent resident of the U.S., or graduating from a high school located in the U.S.
